# 2 Chronicles Chapter 34 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** Josiah was eight years old when he became king, and he reigned thirty-one years in Jerusalem.

**2** He did what was right in the LORD's eyes, following the ways of his ancestor David, never turning to the right or to the left.

**3** In the eighth year of his reign, while still young, he began to seek the God of his ancestor David. In his twelfth year he began purging Judah and Jerusalem of the high places, Asherah poles, and carved and cast idols.

**4** Under his direction, the altars of the Baals were torn down. He cut to pieces the incense altars above them, smashed the Asherah poles and the carved and cast images, ground them to dust, and scattered the dust over the graves of those who had sacrificed to them.

**5** He burned the bones of the pagan priests on their own altars, and so he purified Judah and Jerusalem.

**6** He did the same in the towns of Manasseh, Ephraim, and Simeon, as far as Naphtali — and in the ruins around them.

**7** He tore down the altars, crushed the Asherah poles and idols to powder, and cut down all the incense altars throughout the land of Israel. Then he returned to Jerusalem.

**8** In the eighteenth year of his reign, after he had purified the land and the temple, he sent Shaphan son of Azaliah, Maaseiah the governor of the city, and Joah son of Joahaz the recorder to repair the temple of the LORD his God.

**9** They went to Hilkiah the high priest and gave him the money that had been brought into God's temple, collected by the Levite gatekeepers from Manasseh, Ephraim, and the remnant of Israel, as well as from all Judah, Benjamin, and the residents of Jerusalem.

**10** They entrusted it to the supervisors of the work on the LORD's temple, who paid the workers repairing and restoring the building.

**11** They gave money to the carpenters and builders to purchase dressed stone and timber for joists and beams for the buildings the kings of Judah had allowed to fall into ruin.

**12** The workers labored faithfully. Their supervisors were the Levites Jahath and Obadiah (descendants of Merari), and Zechariah and Meshullam (descendants of Kohath). All the Levites who were skilled musicians

**13** supervised the laborers and directed all the workers in every task. Some Levites served as secretaries, officials, and gatekeepers.

**14** While they were bringing out the money stored in the LORD's temple, Hilkiah the priest found the Book of the Law of the LORD given through Moses.

**15** Hilkiah said to Shaphan the secretary, "I've found the Book of the Law in the LORD's temple!" And he gave it to Shaphan.

**16** Shaphan took the book to the king and reported, "Your officials are doing everything they've been assigned.

**17** They've collected the money found in the LORD's temple and turned it over to the supervisors and workers."

**18** Then Shaphan the secretary informed the king, "Hilkiah the priest has given me a book." And Shaphan read from it in the king's presence.

**19** When the king heard the words of the Law, he tore his robes.

**20** He gave these orders to Hilkiah, Ahikam son of Shaphan, Abdon son of Micah, Shaphan the secretary, and Asaiah the king's attendant:

**21** "Go and inquire of the LORD for me and for those remaining in Israel and Judah about what this book says. The LORD's anger that has been poured out on us is great, because our ancestors didn't obey the word of the LORD or do everything written in this book."

**22** Hilkiah and those the king designated went to the prophetess Huldah, wife of Shallum son of Tokhath, son of Hasrah, keeper of the wardrobe. She lived in Jerusalem's Second Quarter. They spoke to her about this.

**23** She said to them, "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Tell the man who sent you to me,

**24** 'This is what the LORD says: I am going to bring disaster on this place and its people — all the curses written in the book that was read to the king of Judah.

**25** Because they have abandoned Me and burned incense to other gods, provoking Me with everything they've done, My anger will be poured out on this place and will not be quenched.'

**26** Tell the king of Judah, who sent you to seek the LORD, 'This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says about the words you heard:

**27** Because your heart was responsive and you humbled yourself before God when you heard what He spoke against this place and its people, and because you humbled yourself before Me and tore your robes and wept before Me — I have heard you, declares the LORD.

**28** I will gather you to your ancestors, and you will be buried in peace. Your eyes will not see all the disaster I am going to bring on this place and its people.'"" They reported her answer to the king.

**29** Then the king called together all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.

**30** He went up to the LORD's temple with all the people of Judah and the residents of Jerusalem, the priests and the Levites — everyone from the least to the greatest. He read aloud all the words of the Book of the Covenant that had been found in the LORD's temple.

**31** The king stood at his place and made a covenant before the LORD — to follow the LORD and keep His commands, statutes, and decrees with all his heart and all his soul, and to obey the words of the covenant written in this book.

**32** He had everyone in Jerusalem and Benjamin pledge themselves to it. The people of Jerusalem lived according to the covenant of God, the God of their ancestors.

**33** Josiah removed all the detestable practices from all the territory belonging to the Israelites, and he required everyone in Israel to serve the LORD their God. Throughout his reign, they did not fail to follow the LORD, the God of their ancestors.


---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **34:3**: Josiah begins seeking God at sixteen — four years before any public action. The Chronicler wants you to know: the reform started in a teenager's heart before it started in the streets.

- **34:14**: They find the Bible in the temple. Think about that. God's word had been so neglected that it was literally lost in God's own house. And when it's found, it changes everything.

- **34:19**: The king hears the Law read and tears his clothes. This is what Scripture is supposed to do: shatter complacency. Josiah hears the distance between God's standards and his nation's reality, and it breaks him.


— PNEUMA
